BIM Staffing Requirements for Infrastructure Projects

Roads, utilities and site works need different BIM skills from buildings. The roles to plan for and what to test.

Infrastructure BIM is not building BIM on a larger site. Roads, utilities and earthworks are modelled in different tools, with different data, and staffing plans need to reflect that.

The core roles

  • Civil 3D engineers build existing ground surfaces, alignments, profiles and corridors, and calculate earthworks.
  • Utilities modelers model water, drainage, power and telecom networks underground and check them against each other.
  • Infrastructure BIM coordinators federate civil, utility and building models and run coordination at interfaces.
  • CAD draftsmen produce plan and profile sheets and authority drawings.
  • BIM managers set standards for very large, often linear, models and data.

How it differs from buildings

Different software

Civil 3D, InfraWorks and survey tools sit alongside Revit and Navisworks. A strong Revit modeler is not automatically productive in Civil 3D.

Survey-driven models

Infrastructure models start from survey data. Staff need to understand coordinate systems, surfaces and survey accuracy.

Linear scale

Corridors run for kilometres. Models are split by chainage and zones, and data management matters as much as geometry.

Authority requirements

Utility and road authorities have their own drawing and submission requirements, which change by location.

What to test when hiring

  1. Building a surface from survey points and a corridor from an alignment
  2. Modelling a utility network with correct inverts and clearances
  3. Producing plan and profile sheets to a given standard
  4. Coordinating civil and building models at the site boundary

ENGISOFT places infrastructure BIM engineers and Civil 3D engineers; published examples include road, utility and site infrastructure projects in the UAE.
